summary:
Astro Vitals is a flask and Python based web application that allows astronauts to monitor their own health on long space missions. It tracks nine indicators: heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar, temperature, sleep, mood, exercise and radiation dose. The app can be fed with sliders or data can be streamed from a simulated wearable feed, and can also receive data from real devices.
It responds to the challenge by making numbers into clear guidance. An interactive body map indicates each area is either green (safe), amber (caution) or red (unsafe); charts display changes in the vitals over time. A NASA Human Research Program hazard is associated with each indicator, and a plain language explanation is provided for each indicator. Radiation limits for station, deep space, Moon or Mars. If the reading is too low or too high, the app provides a brief tip, and if a value is quite out of range, it instructs the astronaut to contact a flight surgeon. Daily check-ins are encouraged with points, streaks and badges!
This is important since the help from Earth is delayed on missions to Moon or Mars. Astronauts must be able to identify issues quickly and easily.
details:
Astro Vitals is a health-monitoring web application intended to enable astronauts to monitor themselves during long duration space missions. It was developed in Python and Flask for the NASA Space Apps Challenge and is based on NASA's Human Research Program space hazards and Canadian Space Agency's radiation monitoring.

Nine indicators that are monitored by astronauts: heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar, body temperature, sleep, mood, exercise, radiation dose. Readings may be slid in and mood faces put on along with automatically streamed from a simulated wearable sensor feed. The app also supports data via an easy-to-use web endpoint from a real device.

The results are displayed on an interactive body map, with each section being marked in a green, amber or red color, and the heart is beating at the logged pulse of the astronaut. Changes are easily noticeable with a health score, radar chart, daily status bars and trend lines. Limits of radiation change to suit the space station, deep space, the Moon or Mars.

If a reading is too low or too high, the app provides a brief tip and if it is well outside of range, it instructs the astronaut to call a flight surgeon. Daily routine keeps engaging with points, levels, streaks and badges.

All of these features combine to provide a system that allows crews to identify issues early, with an easy-to-find solution, even when assistance from Earth is far away.
